Vetoing because the fix as written fork-bombs every commit; a safe version chains to `$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/hooks/pre-commit`, and only option B (drop hooksPath, gitleaks via per-repo pre-commit) actually fixes the stated symptom at the cost of losing the global scan.

J2: The problem is real (dot_gitconfig.tmpl:17 sets a global hooksPath and pre-commit 4.6.2's install refuses with 'Cowardly refusing to install hooks with core.hooksPath set', no flag override), but option A of the fix is broken: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` honors core.hooksPath (verified locally: prints /Users/admin/.config/git/hooks), so the global hook would exec itself in an infinite loop on every commit, and chaining does not lift pre-commit's refusal anyway. Vetoing because the fix as written fork-bombs every commit; a safe version chains to `$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/hooks/pre-commit`, and only option B (drop hooksPath, gitleaks via per-repo pre-commit) actually fixes the stated symptom at the cost of losing the global scan.
